messages:
taylor-csm: Quick heads-up 1 Nebula Labs jumped from steady-state to a large rerank+embed batch during onboarding. They asked for a pre-QBR cost review + options to avoid surprises. Can we assemble a short playbook and actionable guardrails?

nina-finops: Got a 5-day extract. Embeddings 0.9M tokens/day baseline, spiking to 3.2M on 04/04 when they imported legacy vectors. If sustained they blow through the monthly retainer in ~10 days. I'll draft three billing scenarios + a recommended temporary retainer/top-up flow.

ryan-pe: I can run two quick optimizations: 1) reranker early-exit (stop at top-8) experiment, 2) lightweight dimension-reduction on batch imports (downsample to 384 dims). Will run A/B on 500 requests each.

billing-bot: Billing alert: NEBULA (acct_99876) crossed 78% of monthly retainer at 08:12 UTC. Next threshold (90%) will trigger slack ping and optional auto-topup.

olivia-cseng: Customer asked for non-technical slides showing tradeoffs: "keep quality" vs "lower monthly spend" and clear next steps. They also want a one-click recommendation for a temporary 30% retainer bump.

nina-finops: Quick forecast table (paste):
```
Scenario A - baseline (no change): 0.9M avg/day -> ~27M/mo -> est cost $9,000/mo (embeddings + rerank infra)
Scenario B - sustained spike (+250% during onboarding week then taper): approx 42M/mo -> est cost $14,000/mo
Scenario C - with caching + early-exit + dim-reduce: ~18M/mo -> est cost $6,000/mo
Immediate recs: enable prefix + vector cache for imports, set per-route rate-limit for batch-import jobs to 10 reqs/s, offer a one-time retainer top-up option (30% for 14 days) to avoid throttling during migration.
```

taylor-csm: Nice. For the QBR deck let's include: a short timeline showing the spike origin, the three scenarios, recommended short-term action (top-up + cache), and medium-term (committed retainer + ingested-vector hygiene).

ryan-pe: Results from A/B so far: early-exit reduced average tokens-per-rerank request by ~22% with human spot-check on 200 samples showing 92/200 borderline diffs (mostly reordering, customer-facing metrics unaffected). Dim-reduce on 500 vectors reduced storage cost ~28% and embedding recall showed minor drop in 1% of queries. Attaching examples to thread.

olivia-cseng: I'll draft the 5-slide customer-facing deck and a 1-page ops playbook: what to flip in the console, how to set alerts, and phrasing for the retainer top-up. Also will add a short feedback form link to capture Nebula's tolerances for quality vs cost.

billing-bot: Action created: retainer-topup-proposal (id: topup-99876). Will send invoice preview and a 72-hour auto-topup option if customer opts in.

nina-finops: I'll also create automated alerts at 60% (weekly digest), 80% (email + CS slack), 95% (auto-throttle + ops channel). And I'll model a break-even for committed retainer (monthly vs annual) to show in the QBR.

taylor-csm: Perfect. Timeline: workshop Tue 09:30 PT, QBR follow-up Thu. Ryan/Nina/Olivia please drop final numbers, sample diffs, and the playbook link here by EOD today so I can lock slides.

ryan-pe: Dropped A/B CSV and 6 before/after examples (shortened prompts) in the shared folder.

nina-finops: Dropped forecast spreadsheet and an invoice preview for the 30% 14-day top-up.

taylor-csm: Thanks team  let's run the prep checklist in the workshop and capture Nebula's decision on top-up or throttling. TL;DR deliverables for QBR: 1) short spike root-cause, 2) cost scenarios, 3) one-click temp top-up option, 4) operations playbook + alerts, 5) customer feedback link. :white_check_mark:
